selected.title: Her Goodbye Cake Arrived Before She Told Me She Was Leaving
selected.hook: A bakery delivered my girlfriend a goodbye cake. I had no idea she was going anywhere.
selected.voiceover:
A bakery delivered my girlfriend a goodbye cake. I had no idea she was going anywhere.

Lena and I had been together four years, and that morning we'd toured an apartment because our lease ended in November.

That afternoon, a delivery guy rang our bell holding a cake that said, "Good luck in Singapore, Lena!"

I laughed because I assumed her coworkers were messing with her.

She didn't laugh.

After ten seconds of silence, she admitted she'd applied for a job in Singapore six months ago.

Then she told me she'd accepted it last week.

The company had already booked her flight for next month.

I asked why we were touring apartments together if she knew she was leaving.

She said she hadn't decided how to tell me, and wanted one more normal weekend before everything changed.

That hurt, but the next part was worse.

I asked whether she'd planned for me to come.

She said no.

Apparently she'd told the company she was relocating alone because she wanted to discover who she was without building every decision around a relationship.

I actually understand wanting that.

What I don't understand is letting me compare kitchens and commute times while her coworkers were ordering a farewell cake.

Now she says we can try long distance, but she also says she needs freedom and doesn't want promises about when she'll return.

I love her, but that sounds less like long distance and more like a breakup she couldn't say out loud.

Would you try to save this relationship, or consider the secret decision the real goodbye?
selected.youtube_description:
A surprise goodbye cake exposes a life-changing decision his girlfriend has kept secret for months: she accepted an overseas job and already has a flight booked, while still touring apartments with him at home. This relationship drama about career choices, long distance, trust, and hidden future plans asks whether love can survive when one partner makes the biggest decision alone. Would you try long distance after this?
